To evaluate \(i^{11} + i^{111}\), we first need to understand the powers of the imaginary unit \(i\). The powers of \(i\) cycle every four terms as follows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
i^1 &= i, \\
i^2 &= -1, \\
i^3 &= -i, \\
i^4 &= 1, \\
i^5 &= i, \text{ and so on.}
\end{aligned}
\]

This means that \(i^n = i^{n \mod 4}\). We can use this to find \(i^{11}\) and \(i^{111}\):

\[
11 \mod 4 = 3 \implies i^{11} = i^3 = -i,
\]
\[
111 \mod 4 = 3 \implies i^{111} = i^3 = -i.
\]

Therefore, \(i^{11} + i^{111} = -i + (-i) = -2i\).

# Sum the results

print(result)
